messages:
maya: Heads up — noticing big NVMe write spikes on gpu-pool during last night's large-batch run. p99 write latency shot up, ephemeral volumes saturated and the cleaner process OOMed. Logs attached, will paste snippets below. :warning:

ryan: Which nodes exactly? can you paste `iostat -x 1 3` output or `/proc/diskstats`?

maya: nodes: gpu-az2-012, gpu-az2-013, gpu-az2-014. iostat snippet:
```
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await  r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.10  512.20     4.00 5120.00   20.00    12.34 95.1   1.2     95.9    0.98  99.9
```
writes are almost all sequential small writes from the batcher cache layer.

ops-jen: saw SMART temp blips earlier but no reallocated sectors yet. Could be write amplification from overlayfs + our snapshotter when the batcher churns model shards.

sre-oncall: saw kubelet eviction traces: `oom_kill: cleanup_worker` and a few pods with `corrupt index` in `/tmp/model-cache/0001.idx`. Rolling restart of the node freed up space but left some corrupted cache files.

infra-bot: Note: batch-runner v2 triggered 00:12 UTC with concurrency=16 on gpu-pool (auto-notify).

ryan: Immediate mitigation: reduce batcher concurrency and batch size. Suggested changes we pushed to staging: `--batch-size=8 --concurrency=2 --snapshot=false` and `--model-cache-ttl=60s` to reduce churn. Also throttle IO at the host using `tc qdisc`? (typo, meant `blkio cgroup` limits).

maya: Applied the batcher throttles on a small canary subset (5 pods). iops dropped ~60% and p99 write latency went down to ~12ms. Cleaner stopped OOMing.

ops-jen: If this keeps happening we should consider an in-memory hot cache (tmpfs) for recent prefixes to avoid constant small writes to NVMe. Memory cost vs NVMe wear tradeoff — cc: finance later. :money_with_wings:

ryan: Quick numbers: rough estimate — 4GB tmpfs per pod for hot cache reduces writes by ~40% for these workloads. Cost = 4GB * num-pods memory; cheaper than replacing NVMe every few months. We'll run a canary with tmpfs on 20 pods.

maya: Running tmpfs canary now and kicking off a scrub: `for d in /dev/nvme?n1; do smartctl -a $d | egrep "Reallocated|Temperature|Media"; done` and `ndctl list` to ensure namespaces are ok.

ops-jen: Also adding an alert: nvme write throughput > 400MB/s sustained for >2m AND cleaner OOMs -> page the oncall.

ryan: Follow-ups: (1) add write-amplification metric (bytes_written_by_dev / app_layer_writes) to infra metrics, (2) add snapshotter backoff when IO pressure detected, (3) evaluate tmpfs canary results and cost.

maya: I'll collect metrics (iops, bytes written, p99 latency, cleaner mem) and open an incident for tracking. If canary looks good will roll to prod. tagging @sre-oncall for postmortem and runbook updates.

sre-oncall: Ack. I'll create an incident ticket, add the alert, and draft a short runbook for batcher throttles + tmpfs fallback.

maya: Thanks — will post follow-up numbers shortly. :thumbsup:
